findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a food handler use their phone with gloved hands. CORRECTED- education was conducted about times to wash hands. Hands must be washed after (but not limited to) any of the following activities: touching a personal electronic device, using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, and after touching anything that may contaminate hands. Educate staff regularly about times to wash hands and proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: THIRD REPEAT: Inspector observed single use to-go bowls submerged in a 5 gallon buckets of soy sauce, tea, and sugar (for use as a scoop). The inspector informed the person in charge (PIC) that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the ready to eat (RTE) food items. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup bowl with a gloved hand. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future. Utensils used for RTE foods, ice, and sauces must have a distinction between food contact and hand contact surfaces to prevent bare hands contamination. Due to the fact that this violation has been noted for four consecutive inspections, a follow up date is scheduled for 7/22 with the SCDPH Food Program Supervisor to conduct education.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw chicken stored over raw beef in the grill protein cooler. CORRECTED- items were rearranged to reflect proper storage order. Beef must be cooked to 155F, and chicken must be cooked to 165F to eliminate pathogens that may cause food-borne illness.  Ensure all foods in cooling units are stored in a manner to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the front baffles of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the baffles were wiped with a sanitizer cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of any debris. Food contact surfaces must be maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an accumulation of rust on the shelves of the walk in cooler. Discussed either cleaning/ repainting, or replacing the shelves. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and designed to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.[C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed personal items for staff stored above items for service in the sliding beverage cooler at the entry to the sushi station. Education was conducted regarding the storage of personal items. Personal items should be stored below items for service to prevent potential contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chili sauce on the sauce line to have an internal temperature of 50F. CORRECTED- ice was added to the cold holding unit, and temperature went down to 44F. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (sauces made in house or labeled “refrigerate after opening”) are held at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: It was observed that the unit cold holding sauces cannot maintain sufficient temperatures for cold holding ingredients. CORRECTED- ice was added below the sauces. Include this table in your cold holding operations (adding ice multiple times a day) moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The kitchen hand washing sink (nearest the dish machine) was observed to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- the PIC brought napkins to the area for hand drying. Ensure hand washing sinks are stocked with paper towels at all times to allow for hand drying, and use of a barrier to turn off the faucet.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector probed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods on the cold buffet line and observed internal temperatures over 41F (pork at 45F, dark meat chicken at 48F, light meat chicken and 46F, and beef at 45F). The inspector returned after about 20 minutes and the temperatures did not decrease. CORRECTED- items were moved under time as control (a post-it was placed, indicating foods must be used or discarded by 7PM). Ensure TCS foods are held EITHER at or below 41F, OR used or discarded within 4 hours of being moved out of cold holding units (41F or below) to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The cold holding unit on the buffet line is failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. Ensure the unit is serviced so that foods have an internal temperature at or below 41F. Equipment must have the capacity to cold hold foods at or below 41F. Inspector will return on or by May 11 to verify compliance.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an employee wash hands and turn off the faucet without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the operator informed the new employee about proper hand washing technique. The employee rewashed their hands, using a barrier to turn off the faucet, and therefore prevent re-contaminating hands. Frequently review proper hand washing technique with all staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.

findings.comment: Inspector observed raw fish stored over cabbage in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- items were rearranged to reflect proper storage order.  Ensure all RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins to prevent the contamination of RTE foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the soda nozzles nearest the sushi station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed and brought to the dish area to undergo full ware-washing (wash-rinse-sanitize). Discussed using a brush to clean the nozzles or bringing them for complete ware-washing to remove any soil debris. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items on the cold buffet line to be out of temperature. The PIC verified they had been on the line since the start of service (approximately 2.5 hours):
1) Pork- internal temperature of 45F
2) Crab meat- internal temperature of 50F.
3) Garlic sauce- internal temperature of 47F.
CORRECTED- items were removed from the line and voluntarily discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are cold held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed tuna in reduced oxygen packaging thawing in the sushi cooler. The label indicates that the food must be removed from a reduced oxygen environment upon thawing. CORRECTED- education was conducted and a cut was placed in the package. Ensure all fish in reduced oxygen packaging are vented when moved into thawing to prevent the growth of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Wet cloths were observed stored in an otherwise clean, unused rice cooker. The PIC indicated that these cloths were held for use while storing cooked rice in the rice cooker to help maintain moisture and keep rice from drying out. Discussed wet cloth storage- ensure damp cloths are stored in sanitizer solution, or if used to wipe up a spill, placed in a dirty laundry basket.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and designed to be smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed soap and steel wool in the basin of the hand washing sink at the sushi station. CORRECTED- soap and steel wool were moved to the dump sink. Discussion was had regarding the availability of hand washing sink. The hand washing sink must be available for hand washing ONLY at all times. If the sink is being cleaned, the supplies used to clean the sink should only be brought over at that time, from the dish area, and immediately returned. Cleaning the sink must be a separate task from washing hands, so as not to contaminate hands. Cease this practice.

(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed three cans in the facility’s dry storage to contain significant dents. Two cans of soy sauce contained large dents along the body, and one can of water chestnuts contained a large dent along the top seam. CORRECTED- cans were moved into a cardboard box to be returned to the supplier. PIC stated this should be standard practice (checking for dented cans and moving to cardboard box to receive credit from food supplier). Remind kitchen staff of this practice. Inspector provided dented can infographic to the PIC, and will spot check for dented cans with the employee health educator before the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken stored above RTE sauce in the sliding grill cooler (against the wall). CORRECTED- chicken was moved to the bottom shelf on the other side of the cooler. Ensure all RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins to prevent the contamination of RTE foods and sauces.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Two sanitizers bucket at the grill contained a low concentration of Chlorine bleach sanitizer (0 and 10 ppm respectively).
CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer buckets to (0->100 ppm [bucket behind grill] and 10->200 ppm Cl [bucket across hot holding]) an acceptable sanitizing concentration. Monitor sanitizer concentration with facility’s test strips. Ensure sanitizer is at the concentration recommended by the manufacture’s label, and made ONLY with EPA-labeled bleach and water.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometer in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC moved an ambient thermometer from the walk in freezer to the walk in cooler- near the door. Ensure all cooling units contain ambient thermometers near the warmest part of the unit to monitor proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a fly strip above covered soy sauce and a box of unwashed produce on the cookline. Discussion took place with the PIC regarding proper placement of fly strips (away from areas of food preparation and food storage). Ensure insect control devices are placed in locations that prevent the possible contamination of ready to eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: A leak was observed from the plumbing under the hand washing sink in the dish area. CORRECTED- PIC tightened a fitting, and the pipe was observed to no longer be leaking. Ensure all plumbing is maintained to prevent leaks and convey wastewater out of the facility.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas of the physical facility in need of repair:
1) The caulking on the wall to the right of the dish machine is fragmented. 
2) There are a few small holes from previous shelving on the wall to the right of the dish machine.
3) The hand washing sink nearest the walk in cooler is beginning to separate from the wall (on the left side).
Ensure all surfaces are sealed and repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry of water and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
There were multiple instances where TCS food is not being held at 41F and under: 

1. There was a container of spicy mayo by the sushi bar. This is a sauce that is made in-house and is made with mayonnaise. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that this has likely been sitting out for days and voluntarily discarded it. All sauces made in-house should be held at 41F and under (and should be date marked). 
2. The walk-in cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 48F. The PIC stated that there was a company that fixed the fans yesterday. Upon further investigation, the walk-in cooler had been set this high since yesterday. CORRECTED- The PIC re-set the temperature to 37F and the temperature dropped down to under 41F. The following items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC that had been in the cooler since yesterday: 5 containers of 5 pounds of peeled garlic (probed at 46.5F, 46.4F, 47.4, 46.6, and 46.4), approximately 1300 eggs (8 containers of 180 eggs that probed at 48.3F, 47F, 47F, 47F, 49.7F, 46.4F, 46.9F, and 47.6F), and 56 containers of tofu (5 boxes each containing 12 blocks of tofu that probed to be at 46.4F, 46.3F, 46.5F, 46.3F, and 46.5F). All other items were allowed to be kept due to being delivered today, prepped today, or were sauces that were acidic enough to inhibit bacterial growth.
Ensure that TCS items are held at 41F or under.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The cold holding buffet line is observed to not be properly holding TCS items at 41F and under. On the line, the following items were probed: pork (52.9F), octopus (48F), crab (53F), sprouts (52F), and noodles (49F). CORRECTED- The noodles and sprouts were replaced on the line. The pork, octopus, and crab were placed on Time as Control and the PIC was told to use them within four hours. The operators stated that items are frequently rotated on the line with fresh product. It was recommended to fill the bottom of the cold holding unit with ice and water to allow the items to reach under 41F until the line can be repaired. 

Ensure that TCS items are held at 41F or under.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no date marking in the facility. When the inspector inquired the dates that the TCS foods were prepared they were told by the PIC that the foods were either prepared today or yesterday. Education occurred about date marking requirements with the PIC. TCS and ready to eat (RTE) foods and sauces being held after the day of service are required to be marked with the date, and used or discarded within 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to thaw shrimp in still water in the kitchen preparation area. CORRECTED- The shrimp were placed in a container and were put under cold running water. The PIC and employee were educated that the only proper forms of thawing are through refrigeration, under cold running water that allows the food to remain at 41F and under, or through the cooking process.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F). [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed single use to-go bowl submerged in a 5 gallon soy sauce bucket being used as a scoop. Inspector informed PIC that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the food item. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment:
There were multiple instances where single-service articles and utensils were exposed to contamination: 

1. The small spoons used for sampling are not all facing the same way and are for consumers to grab themselves. Ensure that these are all placed to be facing the same way- with handles out to prevent bare hand contact with food surfaces.
2. Bowls next to the soup hot holding were not inverted. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted these to protect them from contamination. 
3. The foam single-service cups were not inverted. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted these as well. 

Ensure that all single service articles and utensils, including bowls and plates, are inverted or placed under a shelf to protect the food contact surface from contamination. Utensils used for customer self service should be arranged so that the handle is facing outward.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
There were two milk jugs observed to be cut and in use as rice scoops. This was discussed with the operators and they were educated that scoops used for food should be durable, corrosion-resistant, and able to withstand repeated warewashing. Ensure that these scoops are replaced with proper scoops that are sufficient to be used as a food contact surface. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed two employees using their bare hands to shut off the faucet after washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff follow the adequate hand washing procedures at all times, including using a barrier to prevent recontamination of newly-clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed three dented cans (one oyster sauce and two soy sauce) being stored on the shelves in the dry storage. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. The dented cans were separated to be discarded. Ensure that the package integrity of cans are monitored as canned goods are received or stocked.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the no measurable concentration of the sanitizer in the dish machine. After several adjustments, a new bucket of sanitizer concentrate was connected and the machine primed to get the sanitation solution flowing properly. The chlorine concentration was then observed at 50ppm Cl. Inspectors informed PIC to educate staff to routinely test the dish machine chlorine concentration at the start of day and at the end to catch potential malfunctions early. Ensure that the sanitizer solution is monitored at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
1) The chicken in the cold holding on the customer make line was observed to at 47F (probed). CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and who voluntarily discarded the chicken. 
2) A pan of eggs on the customer make line were observed at 50F (ambient temperature), and stocked above the rim of the pan. CORRECTED- Eggs had been replenished after lunch. The pan of eggs was returned to cold holding to cool, and was replaced with a pan not filled above the rim.
Ensure that the temperature of food items in the cold holding are checked at all times regular frequency to avoid food spoilage. Educate staff to avoid stocking pans in in the cold holding unit above the rim of the pan. This will help keep foods 41F or below throughout.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
A rubber spatula with parts of the food contact surface chipping away was observed hanging in the back next to the triple sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the damaged spatula was discarded. Ensure that utensils use in food prep or items that are food contact surfaces are in good repairs are all times. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of grease and soils buildup on the exterior of the fryers and on the floor underneath. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the buildup will be clean. Ensure that the equipment and other kitchen surfaces are routinely cleaned to avoid the accumulation of grease and soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
4th REPEAT: Food handler certificates were not available for all food employees present. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees who handle or prepare food.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towels were not available at the handwashing sink near the dish area. CORRECTED- PIC provided paper towels. Ensure towels are available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The back prep area handsink was observed with plastic containers in the basin. Ensure handsinks are always empty and accessible to facilitate frequent handwashing. CORRECTED- Items were removed and carts were relocated to make handsinks accessible.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3rd REPEAT: 1) Raw chicken was observed stored above raw lettuce and raw beef in the grill area 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged. Signage is posted on the side of the cooler detailing the proper storage order. Label shelves to promote proper storage order. Educate employees on safe storage.
2) Raw calamari was observed thawing above produce in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Calamari was moved to thaw away from vegetables.
Reviewed proper storage order with PIC. Storage was rearranged to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
An open employee beverage was observed stored on the prep counter where an employee was cutting carrots. Ensure employee beverages are in containers with lids and straws and are stored below or away from foods and prep surfaces for service.
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
3rd REPEAT: Food handler certificates were not available for all food employees present. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees who handle or prepare food.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
The CFM present at the beginning of the inspection has not completed allergen awareness training. A CFM with allergen training arrived after the inspection began. Ensure CFMs complete allergen training. Keep certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: An employee was observed rinsing a container and utensils in the back handsink. CORRECTED- Provide education to employees. Handsinks are to be used ONLY for handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw chicken was observed stored above raw vegetables in the grill area 2 door cooler. Corrected- Storage was rearranged. Label shelves to promote proper storage order. Educate employees on safe storage.
Reviewed proper storage order with PIC. Storage was rearranged to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The sanitizer bucket in the sushi area was observed with no measurable Cl concentration. CORRECTED- PIC added bleach to the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed at 100ppm. Educate employees on using Cl test strips to check sanitizer concentration. Ensure sanitizer bucket are 50-200ppm Cl, and that only chlorine is used (no soap should be added to sanitizer solutions).
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Multiple priority and priority foundation violations observed, including storage to prevent cross contamination, cold holding, thawing, and poor handwashing procedure. Ensure staff and PIC are knowledgable about the equipment they are using. Educate staff on proper food handling and storage.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The person in charge present at the beginning and end of this inspection is not a CFM. A CFM arrived midway through the inspection but had to leave prior to completion. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff and scheduled to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Multiple employees were observed improperly washing hands. Technique is not being educated. See that staff is using a barrier to properly turn off the faucet and that soap is being used to scrub hands for 20 seconds. A number of staff were observed washing hands and then turning off the faucet. There is a definite need to educate on hand washing each and every day AND to address and correct as you see an error occur. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed with PIC, who educated employees as issues were observed during this inspection. Continue to educate employees on proper handwashing.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1) The sushi handsink was found with several plastic containers in the basin.
2) The front grill handsink was observed blocked by a cart.
3) The back prep area handsink was observed blocked by a cart and with utensils and plastic containers in the basin.
Ensure handsinks are always empty and accessible to facilitate frequent handwashing. CORRECTED- Items were removed and carts were relocated to make handsinks accessible.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: 1) Raw meats were observed stored above vegetables and sauces in the grill area 2 door cooler. 
2) Raw chicken was observed stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler.
3) Raw shrimp was observed stored above vegetables in the walk-in cooler.
Reviewed proper storage order with PIC. Storage was rearranged to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The sanitizer bucket in the sushi area was observed with no measurable Cl concentration. CORRECTED- Employee remade the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed with a concentration of 200ppm. Educating employees on using Cl test strips to check sanitizer concentration. Ensure sanitizer bucket are 50-200ppm Cl, and that only chlorine is used (no soap should be added to sanitizer solutions).
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) Tofu in the beverage cooler was observed at 66F (probed). CORRECTED- Tofu was voluntarily discarded. No other TCS foods were stored in this cooler.
2) Crab in the top of the kitchen cookline prep cooler was observed at 49F (probed). CORRECTED- Crab was voluntarily discarded. Other foods in the cooler were at or below 41F.
3) Raw beef on the bowl-building line was observed at 49-51F (probed). CORRECTED- Beef was voluntarily discarded. Other foods on the bowl counter were at or below 41F.
Monitor foods to ensure they are held at 41F or below. Minimize time food spends out of temperature control during preparation and keep coolers closed as much as possible.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Three colanders of shrimp, intended to be thawing under running water, were observed at 45-76F (probed). CORRECTED- One bowl, observed at 45F, was moved to the walk-in cooler. The other two bowls were voluntarily discarded. Thaw foods under COOL running water and monitor so thawing foods do not exceed 41F.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Spray bottles were observed unlabeled in the wait station areas (near the sushi area and near the dish machine). Ensure working containers of chemicals are labeled to indicate their contents.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Multiple containers of cooling noodles were observed tightly covered in plastic wrap and stacked in the walk-in cooler. PIC rearranged pans into a single layer. If there is no risk of overhead contamination, keep cooling foods uncovered.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Boxes of food were observed stored on the floor of the walk-in freezer. Store foods at least 6 inches above the ground to prevent potential contamination and facilitate cleaning.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Debris accumulation was observed under equipment in the back cookline. Clean under equipment.
2) Ice accumulation was observed on the inside of the walk-in freezer. Remove ice and prevent accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Food handler certificates were not available for all food employees present. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees who handle or prepare food.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
The person in charge present at the beginning and end of the inspection is not a CFM and has not completed allergen training. A CFM with allergen training arrived midway through the inspection but had to leave prior to completion. Ensure CFMs complete allergen training. Keep certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) Multiple employees are observed improperly washing hands. Technique is not being educated. See that staff is using a barrier is properly turn off the faucet and that soap is being used to scrub hands for 20 seconds. A number of staff are observed rinsing fingers or washing hands and then turning off the faucet and wiping hands on their shirts. Discussed with operator. There is a definite need to educate on hand washing each and every day AND to address and correct as you see an error occur. 
FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Multiple priority and priority foundation violations observed, including storage to prevent cross contamination, thawing, and bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods. Ensure staff and PIC are knowledgable about the equipment they are using. Educate staff on proper food handling and storage.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Signed reporting agreements are not available for kitchen employees present during this inspection. Ensure all employees review and sign the employee reporting agreement. Keep signed agreements on file for review during inspections. (Previously observed during the 12/15/23 inspection.)
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
PICs could not locate the vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Inspector emailed the policy to PIC to be printed and kept on file. 
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Employee was observed cutting cucumber (for use in sushi) with their bare hands. CORRECTED- Provided education and discussed with PIC. Bare hands cannot be used to handle ready-to-eat foods. Ensure clean gloved hands are used to prepare ready-to-eat foods.
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Raw chicken, beef, and fish were observed stored above cilantro and other produce in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage to prevent cross contamination.
Reviewed proper storage order. Rearrange storage to prevent cross contamination. (Previously observed at the 12/15/23 inspection.)
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Can opener observed with soil debris accumulation on the blade. CORRECTED- Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Maintain food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch. (Previously observed at the 12/15/23 inspection.)
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer buckets near the sushi area and wait station were observed with no measurable Cl concentration. CORRECTED- PIC added bleach to each bucket, bringing the concentration to 200ppm. Discussed educating employees on using Cl test strips to check sanitizer concentration. Ensure sanitizer bucket are 50-200ppm Cl.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
ROP (vacuum packaged) tuna was observed sealed in its original packaging and thawing in the walk-in cooler. The label indicated to remove the fish from its packaging prior to thawing under refrigeration. PIC cut all the thawing packages of tuna. Ensure ROP fish is thawed according to its label instructions.
3-501.13: (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Octopus and shrimp were observed thawing in prep sinks in still water. CORRECTED- Discussed thawing methods with PIC, who moved the foods to containers and turned on the faucet to continue thawing under cool running water. 
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration, (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Damp cloths were observed on countertops throughout the facility. Store damp cloths submerged in sanitizer solution, or use to wipe up a spill and send to be laundered. (Previously observed during the 12/15/2023 inspection.)
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A knife was observed stored in a small gap between the two prep cooler lids. The gap is too small to be appropriately cleaned. The knife was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Discussed appropriate storage locations.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
A cloth was observed stored on top of the sushi rice in its warmer in contact with the rice. Cease use of cloths in contact with the cooked sushi rice. Ensure that food contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. CORRECTED- The cloth was removed from the sushi rice.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Seal bare wood shelves at the sushi station. (Previously observed at the 12/15/23 inspection.)
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulk along the dirty dish drainboard was observed to have an accumulation of black mold. Clean caulking.
2) Excessive crumb accumulation was observed below the dry storage shelves. Sweep under equipment.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Employee foods were observed stored among foods for service in the beverage coolers and in the prep cooler. Employee personal foods and drinks need to be stored in designated areas below and away from foods for service.
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Food handler certificates were not available for all food employees present. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees who handle or prepare food.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Neither CFM has completed allergen training. Complete ANSI-approved allergen training. Keep certificates on file. (Previously observed at the 12/15/23 inspection.)
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Multiple priority and priority foundation violations observed, including a complete lack of sanitizer solution prepared throughout the facility, lack of up to date sushi pH logs and familiarity with the equipment used to check the pH, and other violations detailed below. Ensure staff and PIC are knowledgable about the equipment they are using. Educate staff on proper food handling and storage.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed reporting agreements are not available for all employees present during this inspection. Ensure all employees review and sign the employee reporting agreement. Keep signed agreements on file for review during inspections.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to quickly rinse hands, then turn the faucet off without using a barrier. Briefly reviewed proper handwashing technique with PIC. Ensure all employees are educated and practice good handwashing, taking time to scrub hands, then using a paper towel to turn the faucet off.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee began to don gloves after handling pH calibration chemicals without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector had PIC interrupt the employee and remind them to wash their hands. Employees must wash hands upon entering the kitchen, before donning gloves, and after any activity that may have contaminated hands.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Sushi area handwashing sink contained a spatula and a plastic container when inspector arrived. CORRECTED- PIC moved items from the handwashing sink. Keep handsinks clear and accessible at all times.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Six severely dented cans observed in the dry storage area (3 cans of water chestnuts, 1 pineapple, and 2 soy sauce). PIC will return the dented cans to the supplier. Return dented cans to the supplier. If a can becomes dented while stocking, it may be opened immediately for use, but cannot be kept to use at a later time.
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1) Scallops and crab observed stored above onions in the walk-in cooler.
2) Chicken observed stored above shrimp in the 2 door grill cooler.
Reviewed proper storage order. Rearrange storage to prevent cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Can opener observed with soil debris accumulation on the blade. CORRECTED- Can opener was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Maintain food contact surfaces clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
At the bowl-building counter, raw shell eggs observed stored at 50-60F, and crab was observed at 52F, probed. Other foods in the same cold holding units were observed at 42F or below. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were removed from service. Eggs were kept for personal use. Crab was discarded.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP
findings.comment:
pH logs have not been recorded since 12/10. pH meter does not appear to work and staff are unsure how to fix it. Time as a control will be used for sushi rice until the pH meter is functional. Sushi rice must be used or discarded within 4 hours of being made. Record prep time and/or discard time on a paper or sticky note at the sushi station.
8-103.12: If AUTHORITY grants VARIANCE, PERMIT HOLDER shall: (A) comply with HACCP PLAN (P) (B) Maintain and provide records. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility does not have any probe thermometers. Provide probe thermometers for use monitoring temperatures in the kitchen.
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.comment:
Damp cloths were observed on countertops throughout the facility. Store damp cloths submerged in sanitizer solution, or use to wipe up a spill and send to be laundered.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility does not have any sanitizer solution prepared. Sanitizer solution should be prepared before beginning any food handling or prep. CORRECTED- Sanitizer buckets were prepared.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

findings.comment:
1) Seal wall around the pipe in the mop sink area.
2) Seal bare wood at the sushi station.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]
